coverageScope.summary: ASARD supports compliance with the listed controls for the runtime chat-ACL sharing plane (plane #1) only. Coverage is detection-based; remediation is staged behind a human approval (Flow B) and its runtime enforcement is documented as a design boundary, not empirically measured. ASARD does not by itself satisfy any control in isolation.
gaps: Plane #2 - authoring share (PrincipalObjectAccess Editor/Viewer rows): not enumerated or remediated.
Plane #3 - M365 Copilot Agent Store / Teams 'Built for your org': out of scope, governed in the M365 Admin Center.
Remediation runtime (Flow B) is staged behind a human approval; its enforcement is a documented boundary, not an empirically measured result.

Canonical-zone reconciliation (Coordinator Decision 'Option A', 2026-06-13): earlier ASARD releases keyed the environment-name classifier inversely (enterprise -> Zone 3, personal -> Zone 1), so an enterprise environment was classified Zone 3 and persisted as fsi_zone=100000003. The per-zone sharing-policy gradient was already canonical (Zone 1 = strictest = no group sharing permitted), but the zone LABELS were inverted (Zone 1 labelled 'Personal Productivity', Zone 3 labelled 'Enterprise/Regulated'). The canonical agent-intake schema and the live lab-tenant fsi_acv_zone set define Zone 1 (Enterprise)=100000001=most restrictive, Zone 2 (Team)=100000002, Zone 3 (Personal)=100000003=least restrictive, Unclassified=100000000. This release flips the name classifier to enterprise/prod -> Zone 1 and personal/dev -> Zone 3 and corrects the RegulatoryContext labels in both the PowerShell resolver (Get-ExpectedSharingPolicy.ps1) and the Python engine (asard_zone_rules.py); the already-canonical zone->integer write-back (Zone 1 -> 100000001) is unchanged, and a gated canonical-zone unit assertion (strictest policy <=> Zone 1 <=> 100000001) is locked. The live-validated fixture row resolved to Unclassified=100000000, whose no-group-sharing policy is unchanged by this remap, so that specific run's Failed/Critical outcome was and remains correct. For name-classified environments, however, this remap CHANGES the effective policy tier - it is a behavioral change, not merely a stored integer/label flip. Because the per-zone sharing policy is keyed off the RESOLVED zone and this release flips the environment-name classifier, an enterprise/prod-named environment moves from Zone 3 (group sharing permitted, lenient) to Zone 1 (no group sharing, strictest), and a personal/dev-named environment moves from Zone 1 (strictest) to Zone 3 (least restrictive), correcting a prior inversion that applied over-strict policy to personal-named environments and under-strict policy to enterprise-named environments. This is the canonically-correct behavior - fail-safe stricter for enterprise-named environments and a relaxation for personal-named environments - so operators should re-run the solution after upgrading and review any name-classified environments whose effective tier changes. This is a code-and-text-only remap and was NOT re-validated against a live tenant; correctness is established by (1) the canonical-zone unit assertion, (2) static gates (PowerShell parse + PSScriptAnalyzer + py_compile + valid JSON), and (3) byte-for-byte alignment with the four lab-validated sibling solutions (FUS, CMM, GAC, ACA) flipped identically and live-validated on the lab validation tenant 2026-06-13. Historical fsi_zone rows from earlier releases carry pre-canonical integers/labels and are retained unaltered; operators should re-run the solution after upgrading to refresh persisted integers (no auto-migration of historical rows). ASARD supports compliance with Controls 1.18 and 2.8; it does not by itself ensure, guarantee, or eliminate regulatory risk.

controls.notes: Supports compliance with Application-Level Authorization / RBAC expectations by detecting agent chat-ACL sharing posture (bot.accesscontrolpolicy + bot.authorizedsecuritygroupids) against per-zone approved-security-group policy (plane #1 only). Remediation is staged behind a human approval (Flow B). Does not by itself satisfy the control; planes #2/#3 are not covered.

Supports compliance with Access Control / Segregation-of-Duties expectations by routing non-compliant chat-ACL sharing through an approval-gated remediation (plane #1 only). The access change is applied only after a separate human approval (Flow B); runtime enforcement is documented as a design boundary, not empirically measured. Does not by itself satisfy the control; planes #2/#3 are not covered.
